ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Hybrid non-rigid Transformation-based Normalizing Flows for Efficient Boltzmann Sampling
PROPOSAL: 
We propose a novel architecture for normalizing flows that incorporates non-rigid transformations to learn flexible and efficient deformations of the input space. Our method combines the strengths of both rigid flow-based methods and non-rigid transformations, enabling it to tackle challenging tasks such as sampling from complex Boltzmann distributions. We introduce a novel transformation module that learns to adaptively apply non-rigid transformations to the input space, allowing for efficient generation of Boltzmann samples.
CONTROLS: Original proposal 3, standard rigid flow-based normalizing flows, empirical inverse E-step.
COST: 1,800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed hybrid method outperforms traditional rigid flow-based methods in terms of both sample quality and efficiency, while remaining computationally tractable and scalable for large molecular systems.

TITLE: Kernel-based Importance Sampling for Boltzmann Generators
PROPOSAL: 
We develop a kernel-based importance sampling ( KBS ) framework for Boltzmann generators, which enables efficient estimation of the Boltzmann weights for samples produced by the generator. Our approach uses a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) to model the high-dimensional energy landscape of the molecular system, allowing for a sophisticated treatment of the correlations between energy and configuration space. By leveraging the kernel trick, KBS achieves an efficient computation of the Boltzmann weights, which can be used to correct the samples produced by the generator.
CONTROLS: Original proposal 1, KBS without the encoder-decoder architecture, empirical inverse E-step.
COST: 2,000 GPU-hours

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Mixture of Volumetric Transformations for Efficient Boltzmann Sampling
PROPOSAL: 
We propose a new architecture for normalizing flows that combines a mixture of volumetric transformations to efficiently cover the complex energy landscape of molecular systems. Our approach introduces a probabilistic framework for selecting and combining centroid Gaussian mixtures, which enables the direct estimation of the energy landscape without requiring an explicit representation of the target distribution. This allows for efficient sampling from complex Boltzmann distributions, while reducing the computational cost associated with traditional flow-based methods.
CONTROLS: Original proposal 2, importance sampling correction of mixtures with estimated densities
COST: 2,200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed mixture of volumetric transformations achieves state-of-the-art results in terms of both sample quality and efficiency, demonstrating its applicability to challenging molecular systems.

ACTION: REVISE 6
TITLE: Mixture of Volumetric Transformations for Efficient Boltzmann Sampling
PROPOSAL: 
We extend the proposal 6 by incorporating a novel hierarchical clustering algorithm to optimize the mixture components of the volumetric transformations. This allows for adaptive selection of the most relevant mixture components, which improves the efficiency of the sampling process. Additionally, we investigate the use of a learnable, probabilistic assignment mechanism to dynamically reallocate the mixture components during training, leading to further improvements in sample quality and convergence.
CONTROLS: Original results from proposal 6, hierarchical clustering without probabilistic assignment mechanism.
COST: 2,500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By incorporating the hierarchical clustering algorithm and the probabilistic assignment mechanism, we expect to achieve significant improvements in sample quality and convergence rate, making the Mixture of Volumetric Transformations an even more competitive method for Boltzmann sampling.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Scalable Training of Boltzmann Generators via Conditional Normalizing Flows
PROPOSAL: 
We present a novel approach for training Boltzmann generators using conditional normalizing flows (CNFs). Our method leverages the expressiveness of CNFs to learn complex conditional distributions that approximate the underlying Boltzmann distribution. We demonstrate that our approach can be used to train large-scale Boltzmann generators, enabling the efficient sampling of complex molecular systems.
CONTROLS: Original proposals 1, 3, 4, and 6, CNFs without conditioning on the Boltzmann distribution.
COST: 3,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed method for training Boltzmann generators using CNFs shows promising results in terms of sample quality and efficiency, making it a competitive approach for complex molecular systems.
